radiology_report:
Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede) — Radiology Division
Date: 10 January 2025
Modality: Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation of prior prostate cancer diagnosis; current PSA 4.7 ng/mL.

FINDINGS: Prostatic volume registers at 33.46 mL. T2-weighted sequences reveal a homogeneous intermediate signal across the peripheral zone. An ill-defined 9 mm focus occupies the left mid-gland peripheral zone, displaying slightly reduced T2 signal without definitive capsular involvement. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates no appreciable restriction, with unremarkable b-value correlation. Dynamic contrast-enhanced phases show no early or focal enhancement. Seminal vesicles maintain normal dimensions and signal characteristics. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous abnormalities are detected.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 2 lesion located in the left mid-gland peripheral zone. Prostate volume 33.46 mL; PSA density 0.14 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.59620297.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: 15 September 2024 — Dr. C. Peters (GP): Routine follow-up conducted today. Following an initial reading of 4.4 ng/mL in early 2023, a repeat assay confirmed a PSA value of 4.7 ng/mL. Considering the documented biopsy history alongside this upward trajectory, a referral to the urology outpatient department has been processed for specialist reassessment.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: 23 July 2023 — Dr. C. Peters (GP): Consultation focused on ongoing PSA surveillance. The latest measurement recorded 3.1 ng/mL, remaining stable relative to the prior year. Annual monitoring protocols were reiterated, alongside a discussion regarding urinary symptoms and alcohol consumption. A follow-up PSA appointment was arranged for the coming months.
